title: Transactionized ingest SLI shadow-tests and budgeted trace-retention playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our analytics ingest pipeline is the largest driver of observability cost and the primary source of noisy SLI signals for Console. We need a repeatable playbook to validate SLI changes and tracing / sampling adjustments without impacting production users or blowing our trace budget.

Goal: Create a transaction-scoped approach to shadow-testing SLI and sampling changes, plus a cost-constrained trace retention strategy that preserves investigatory signal for high-risk transactions while lowering median retention for low-value events. The playbook will: (1) define transactional SLIs/SLOs and acceptance gates, (2) implement shadow-run harnesses and synthetic replays for candidate ingest changes, (3) define per-transaction retention tiers and eviction rules, and (4) provide dashboards/alerts to measure both correctness and $/million-events cost impact.

Background & motivation: We already have tenant-prioritized SLO work (see ENG-33109) and synthetic probes (ENG-67891). However, previous efforts focused on journey probes and coarse tenant partitions; this ticket focuses on the ingest path as a transaction boundary (e.g., model inference request, embedding write, console-route aggregation). Treating a transaction as the unit allows us to: correlate traces across services reliably, keep high-fidelity traces for transactions that touch critical code paths, and aggressively budget retention for low-significance transactions.

Scope: backend console analytics ingest path (collector -> enrich -> ingest-batch -> write/warehouse), trace & event retention config, synthetic replay harness, dashboards and alerts. Does NOT include long-term analytic pipelines (OLAP/warehouse tuning) or UI changes besides dashboards.

Design overview: 
- Transactionization: add/ensure transaction_id and transaction_type tags are present at collector (if missing, synth wrapper will enrich). Transaction types mapped to retention tiers: critical, standard, ephemeral.
- SLIs: (a) ingest-success-rate (per-transaction-type, per-tenant) measured at write acknowledgement, (b) P99 end-to-end latency from collector accept -> write ack, (c) trace-linkage-rate (percentage of successful transactions that have an associated trace span with full parent chain).
- SLO targets & alert thresholds: ingest-success-rate >= 99.95% (rolling 30d), P99 latency < 800ms (rolling 7d) for critical transactions, trace-linkage-rate >= 98% for critical, >= 90% for standard. Alert severity tiers tied to customer_impact label.
- Shadow testing: route a copy of production traffic to a candidate ingest pipeline with alternate sampling & retention configs. Shadow traffic must be write-only (no mutations) and annotated with a shadow-run tag. The candidate pipeline writes to a temporary store and emits metric deltas (sli_diff, retention_bytes_estimate).
- Synthetic replay harness: a replay job that replays a day of sampled production transactions at higher temporal density to stress test caching, kernel scheduling, and retention rules. Output used to validate SLOs under synthetic higher-throughput conditions.
- Budgeted retention scheme: define per-transaction retention budget buckets (critical: 30d full traces, standard: 7d truncated traces + full spans for errors, ephemeral: 72h headers-only). Implement probabilistic retention for standard bucket to enforce target storage $/events.
- Observability & dashboards: new console dashboard panels: per-tenant ingest success, transaction-type heatmap (throughput vs P99), shadow-delta rollup, retention-cost estimator, synthetic-replay SLO compare. Include drill-down traces with transaction_id and sample_bucket tags.

Implementation notes & decisions to make: 
- Where to enforce transaction_id: collector vs enrich stage. Prefer collector + a defensive enrich fallback to avoid orphaned traces.
- How to compute retention cost estimate: use bytes emitted to trace-store + estimated compression factor; calibrate with last 30d actuals.
- Trace truncation strategy: keep full root spans and N downstream spans (N configurable) then attach compacted metadata for remaining spans to preserve causal links.
- Sampling & probabilistic retention: use deterministic bucketing (hash(tenant, transaction_id) mod N) to ensure reproducible captures for debugging.

Deliverables: 
- Shadow-run configuration and runner (k8s job) that can be toggled via feature flag.
- Synthetic replay job with deterministic temporal stretching and failure injection knobs.
- Console dashboards and a runbook page documenting SLO gates and rollout criteria.
- Trace retention policy implemented as a configurable policy in the trace-ingest service with per-transaction-type enforcement.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field below.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Cost spike during synthetic replay or shadow tests: cap throughput and run in off-peak windows; track retention_bytes_estimate before longer replays.
- Incomplete transaction tagging: add defensive enrichment and a nightly job to surface untagged transactions.
- False-positive alert noise from early rollouts: use canary thresholds and rolling windows; allow temporary suppression for canaries.

Related artifacts: GitHub PRs and design notes will link into Confluence/Drive. Initial design doc: https://confluence.internal/redwood/console/tx-ingest-retention (placeholder). Temporary perf dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/tx-ingest-shadow (placeholder).
acceptance_criteria: Shadow-run can be enabled and disabled via feature flag without touching prod writes
Shadow-run emits metric comparing candidate pipeline SLI to prod SLI (sli_delta) and retention_bytes_estimate
Synthetic replay can replay 1x/5x/10x sampled day of traffic in staging with failure injection and produce SLO comparison report
Per-transaction retention tiers implemented and enforced in trace-ingest service for critical/standard/ephemeral
Dashboards present: transaction-type heatmap, per-tenant ingest-success, shadow-delta rollup, retention-cost estimator
Runbook captures rollout gates: 0/1/5/25/50/100% canary progression with automated rollback on defined SLI regressions

Implement shadow-run plumbing (message copy, shadow tag, temporary write target)
Build synthetic replay job and test harness in staging
Add per-transaction retention policy in trace-ingest with truncation and probabilistic rules
Create Grafana dashboard panels and drill-down traces with transaction_id filters
Author runbook and acceptance test checklist
Run a controlled shadow-run for 48h and produce cost delta report
comments: 2025-03-10 Asha Patel: Initial ticket created after spike in trace storage costs and missed SLI regression during model-serving rollout. Recommended approach: shadow-testing + retention tiers. Assigned to Miguel for implementation.

2025-03-12 Miguel Ortega: Spike repros in staging using sampled day; initial replay shows a 2.7x increase in P99 under 10x replay. Need to validate batching knobs and kernel selection behavior under synthetic load. Will add failure injection to synthetic harness.

2025-03-14 Design review (Lina Chen): Favor per-transaction bucketing with deterministic hashing. Recommend capturing parent_service and feature_flag context on traces for faster triage. Also requested a mockup of dashboard panels prior to infra changes.

2025-03-16 Security (Ravi Singh): Trace truncation approach approved pending review on PII scrub rules. Need explicit list of fields retained in truncated traces and proof of scrubbing. Marked security_review_required = true.

2025-03-18 Miguel Ortega: Implemented feature flag scaffold and basic shadow-run plumbing in staging. Preliminary shadow-run 6h report attached in attachments. Noted higher retention_bytes_estimate for standard bucket than expected — tuning probabilistic retention scheduled next.
2025-03-18 Asha Patel: Added canary progression plan to runbook and set gating thresholds. Planned 25% canary for next week if standard bucket tuning reduces retention estimate by >=40% in staging.
